title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 56
paragraphs: The Greeks meanwhile at Salamis, when it was announced to them what had happened at the Athenian Acropolis, were so troubled that some of the commanders did not even wait for the question under discussion to be decided, but began hurrying to their ships and putting up their sails, meaning to make off with all speed. Among those who stayed behind it was finally resolved to fight at sea in defense of the Isthmus. Night then came on, and they, having been dismissed from the council, went to their ships.
